title: Statistically-powered AB & Shadowing Orchestrator with Auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an opinionated experimentation orchestrator that makes it easy for product and platform teams to run statistically-powered A/B tests and shadowing runs for model version upgrades, with automatic rollback gates and clear operational playbooks. The feature ties into Redwood Console for exposing traffic, dashboards, and alerts; integrates with the runtime for shadow forwarding and canary traffic splits; and provides a compact set of statistical tests and early-stopping rules suitable for common production metrics (latency P50/P95, token cost, generation quality signals).
acceptance_criteria: Console UX: experiment creation flow supports: target model versions, traffic split (canary, AB), shadow forwarding toggle, cohort stratification fields, and exposure schedule
Powering: the system recommends a minimum sample size and/or exposure ramp based on user-selected primary metric and desired statistical power/confidence
Stat tests: built-in sequential checks (SPRT and group-sequential options) for continuous monitoring and an explicit non-inferiority configuration for failure-mode detection
Auto-rollback: experiments can be configured with automated rollback policies that trigger a rollback when pre-defined statistical and operational thresholds are breached

Observability: experiment dashboard surfaces per-cohort metrics, lift/loss, p-values/Bayes factors, drift signals, and a single-click abort/rollback action that is tied to a GitHub PR and incident ticket template
Shadowing: runtime can mirror live traffic to a variant without impacting user-facing responses and logs are available for offline analysis
Audit: experiment configuration and outcome are recorded in audit logs for compliance and forensics
tasks: Design PRD with example templates for common experiment types (latency-first, cost-first, nli-quality)
Implement backend experiment API to store experiment definitions, exposures, and checkpoints
Extend runtime routing to support mirror (shadow) routes and gradual traffic splitting keyed by route and customer tier
Integrate sequential statistical engine (open-source library evaluation and selection)
Build Console workflow: create/edit experiment, monitor, and action (abort/rollback)
Ship dashboards: per-experiment time series, cohort breakdowns, and automatic highlight of signals that meet rollback conditions
Write rollout playbook and runbook templates for SRE/CS teams
Add e2e tests and gated rollout to Dedicated customers for validation
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Chose sequential testing (SPRT / group-sequential) as default to enable early stopping while preserving operating characteristics
2025-02-13: Non-inferiority framing selected for most production rollouts to reduce false-positive rollbacks on minor metric noise
2025-02-15: Opted to surface both frequentist and Bayesian indicators (p-value + Bayes factor) in the dashboard to aid cross-team interpretation
2025-02-16: Auto-rollback will be opt-in per-experiment with human-in-the-loop notification by default for P0 customers
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha: Draft PRD uploaded; requesting feedback from runtime and SRE teams.
2025-02-12 - Lena Cho (Eng): We'll need to add a per-tenant rate limit for shadowing to avoid KV cache pressure; adding ENG-21843 as dependency.
2025-02-14 - Diego: Proposed default rollback thresholds: 5% increase in P95 latency sustained over 10k requests OR statistically significant drop (alpha=0.01) in primary quality metric.
2025-02-16 - Product review: Agree with sequential tests, but PM asks for simple presets for non-data-scientist users (e.g., 'safety-first', 'cost-optimised').
2025-02-17 - Design: Mockups updated with a compact exposure control slider and preset templates; uploading new figma link.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): expose feature to internal product and SRE teams for validation, run 10 internal canary experiments
Phase 2 (beta): small set of Dedicated customers opt-in; collect telemetry and iterate on thresholds
Phase 3 (public): GA in Console with docs, runbooks, and default presets
Migration: provide a CLI and API for existing experiments to be imported into new orchestrator
metrics: Primary metric: user-defined (examples: completion-quality-score, conversion-rate, safety-flag-rate)
Operational metrics: P50/P95 latency, tokens-per-request, inference error-rate
Statistical signals: p-value / Bayes factor, running power estimate, effective sample size
risks: Misconfigured experiments may cause noisy rollbacks — mitigated via presets and conservative defaults
Shadowing load could increase latency or pressure caches; runtime rate-limits and sampled shadowing required
Users may misinterpret statistical outputs; provide clear inline guidance and recommended actions
Auto-rollback false positives in low-traffic cohorts; require minimum sample size and cohort gating before auto-action
